bibl.title: The Tenth Catechetical Homily— ܡܐܡܪܐ ܕܥܣܪܐ
bibl.author: Theodore of Mopsuestia — ܬܐܕܘܪܘܤ ܡܦܫܩܢܐ

noteGrp.note: On the Holy Spirit (continues), on the Church and final statements of the Creed. The Spirit is called “the Spirit of truth”, as He is of divine nature, immutable and eternal, and He gives eternal benefits. “Who proceeds from the Father” means that the Spirit is inseparable from the Father. “Giver of Life” indicates that the Spirit is God because He is able to grant immortality. The statement on the Church “One Catholic Church” means that a baptized Christian becomes a member of the Church as of one body that has communion with Christ and participation in future benefits. The Church is also called “holy” and “Catholic” because of the holiness given to it by the Holy Spirit and because of its existence in many countries and in all times. The creedal statement “For the remission of sins” shows a benefit of the profession of faith. Remission means here complete abolition of sin. “For the resurrection of the flesh and life everlasting” means that after resurrection, all will become immortal and immutable, and sin will vanish completely.
